I don't remember hearing them specifically *name* Hades' daughter in the trailer, which is important because he has five (two with Persephone who also birthed Zagreus from the first game and three with Nyx who are called the Furies). Looking it up, it's Melinoë who gained aspects of power from both Hades and Persephone.

I haven't played the early access on Steam yet, but the story might make sense with the Titans as Zagreus was tortured/eaten by them, making for a potential tale of vengeance.

To note, Hades' other daughter with Persephone was Makaria whose power aspect is more related to judgement - dividing the valiant from the not. His daughters with Nyx were Alecto (punish moral wrongs), Tisiphone (punish murderers), and Megaera (punish infidelity, theft, and oath-breaking).

I thought it would be a spiritual successor to Armored Core but it ended up just being a bunch of anime cringe. The weapon balance was terrible to the point where the default rifle you start the game with was one of the best weapons and even used by the main antagonist the whole story! Arsenal vs Arsenal combat was ridiculous because everybody is so mobile, even my "these missiles are special because they have super accuracy" homing missile launcher had 8% hit rate after the fight. The big big boss machines that were the ENTIRE POINT of the plot and heavily advertised and dropped the best loot were only fightable in multiplayer mode, and forgotten about in the story. And then even little things like machine guns would only play the firing sound every 6th shot, so you're spraying with what look like Uzis but instead of sounding like "TAKAKAKAKAKAKAKA" they go "blat. blat. blat. blat. blat."

I hope this message finds you well! I wanted to take a moment to share an exciting idea that I believe could enhance the Nintendo Switch 2 experience: integrating a dedicated Nintendo Music Player into the system.

Imagine being able to listen to your favorite Nintendo soundtracks right from the Home Menu! Whether you’re navigating through system settings, browsing the Nintendo Switch Online features, checking out Nintendo news, or enjoying virtual game cards, having a music player would add a wonderful layer of enjoyment to our gaming experience. 

The idea of a Nintendo Music Player is not just about background music; it’s about creating a nostalgic and immersive atmosphere for players of all ages. From the cheerful tunes of classic games to the epic scores of new releases, a built-in music player would allow us to celebrate Nintendo’s rich musical history while we game.

Furthermore, this feature could include curated playlists based on different themes, games, or even special events. Players could easily customize their listening experience, making their time with the Switch 2 even more personal and enjoyable.

Over the last year, I've slowly got into the Yakuza series, and it's already become my favourite video game series, hands down. 

I started with the original Yakuza on PS2, then Like A Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name, then Ishin, and Yakuza O Director's Cut was my launch game for Switch 2.

Some of the things I love about this series is the authentic feeling of the game world, the amount of side activities and minigames, the intense combat and the deep, but sometimes hilarious, story.

Each pedestrian passing by, smoking a cigarette, carrying their shopping, makes me feel like the world is populated by real people. Each shop, restaurant or arcade I pass by, or enter, feels as I'm right there in the city. 

From disco dancing to running a real estate business, playing a game of Outrun in the arcade to teaching a woman how to be a dominmatrix, I'm never bored of things to do outside the main story.

From literally dancing on my opponents, to shoving a traffic cone on their head, the combat is so fun and satisfying.

I was literally in tears at the end of The Man Who Erased His Name. That story hit me hard.

So what I'm basically saying is, I love Yakuza, and I'm looking forward to playing more of the series.

Thanks for supporting Nintendo Switch 2 also. I look forward to more Yakuza on the go! 💗

For those wondering: you don't need to transfer your Switch to Switch 2.

If you want a clean break, with no media captures or rarely-played games cluttering up your system, you can skip the System Transfer and install your old games to Switch 2 on an as-needed basis. With Save Data Cloud and Virtual Game Card, as long as you link up your old Switch with Switch 2 (which is done through a speedy process with your Nintendo Account) you can still play the same game on both systems... but not at the same time.

Of course, once you skip System Transfer, you have to factory reset the Switch 2 to access the feature again.

I will never forget the moment I learned about Iwata's passing. I was playing Splatoon on the WiiU - for anyone who does not know, the 3DS and WiiU had this thing called Miiverse, where you could draw pictures on the gamepad/touch screen and post them. Pictures drawn for the Splatoon game could actually show up in game while you were playing. 

The match started like any other - just a typical Turf War round. I inked my way out to the center and so did the opposing team. 

Splatoon was unique in that you could EASILY tell where people were LOOKING because their character's torso/weapon would be pointed that way. 

Before I could reach the other side... The leading player on the opposing side just... Stopped shooting. They weren't looking at me - they were looking over my character. UP... At the billboard featuring Miiverse art. 

The art was a picture of Iwata with "RIP" written next to it. 

The other players stopped and looked up at it too. We looked around - and nearly all of the artworks featured messages about Iwata. Pictures of Nintendo characters crying beside grave stones. Written quotes from Iwata in both beautiful cursive and messy touchpad scribbles. 

We stopped fighting. One of the players looked at their feet the rest of the match. (I suspect they put their controller down to check if the news was real) 

The match did not resume. We all just... Stood there in the center and shared a moment of silence. 

I don't remember which side won that match, because it definitely felt like we all collectively lost. But I will never forget what happened during that Turf War, because it made a group of complete strangers stop playing the game. 

I don't know of many CEOs who could make that happen.

The Legend of Zelda: Children of the Mask

(A third game in the BotW gameplay style, set in Termina)


After the events of TotK, Zelda is focusing on strengthening foreign alliances so they can help eachother in times of need. As she is discussing plans with Link, a wounded soldier stumbles in, rambling about an attack before he collpases. When he wakes up, he tells you the story. A diplomatic convoy to Termina was attacked by a mask wearing cult, and the ambassador was killed. The leader's mask had glowing red red eyes. Zelda sends Link to Termina to investigate.


The games tutorial section (like the Great Plateau) has Link searching Clock Town and the surrounding areas for clues on the cult. It leads you to four “Masked crypts” or cult hideouts, each with a rune-like mask grabbing you an ability. Afterwards, the mayor gives a speech about the growing dangers in the kingdom. But as he is speaking, the cult attacks and raids the town hall. They steal four seemingly random artifacts, and scatter to the four regions of Termina. The distressed mayor sends you to the Astral Observatory.


At the Observatory, the old man tells you the legend of what once transpired in Termina, and the cults origins. The Masked donned by the cult leader is none other than Majora's Mask. The four artifacts that they stole were fragments of the Mask of Resurrection, a powerful tool that can bring back dead people. If they find a way to put the mask back together, they will use the mask along with Majora's Mask to bring back their master, the dark wizard Majora himself. As it currently stands, they are still finding out how to rebuild it, potentially giving you time to retrieve and destroy the mask fragments if you act fast.


Regional Phenomena Concepts


Woodfall

When you step foot in the jungle, the entire region is overgrown with vines, blocking out the sun and pulling anyone who touches them into the darkness. As you traverse the land, you discover a campsite with the Deku Royals. They have tracked the source of the growth to the Deku Palace. The King wants to aid you on your quest, believing the safety of the kingdom to be his responsibility. You both go through the vines to find his belongings, such as weapons and armor. Then you make your way through to the palace, the next dungeon. But when you enter, you are ambushed and the Deku King is kidnapped by the cult. When you reach the end of the dungeon, you find the cult forcibly putting a mask on the king, a Corrupted Mask (a mask that connects you to the cult leader, forcing you to carry out his will, and enhancing your abilities). He morphs into a giant Deku Gorilla creature, and everything you collected for him becomes a problem, as he swings a club at you, and forcing you to remove his armor before you attack. When you defeat him, before he goes back to normal, he speaks in a possessed voice about a secret altar on the map. This altar has a mural about the dark interlopers. When he goes back to normal, the ground collapses underneath you, revealing the source of the vines, a fragment of the Mask of Resurrection that had been corrupting the ground with it's dark magic.


Snowhead

When you enter the region, you find a group of Goron scavengers scrambling to get to the mountain. It turns out that some of the cult members had been attacking the Goron's dwelling, and one of their warriors went to fight them off. He never came back, and an avalanche blocked off the Goron's entrance. You need to go through an icy cave to get to the rest of the Gorons, and when you do get to them, you need to find a way to clear out the snow. When the snow is cleared, you find the soldier, with a corrupted mask. Ice has taken over his body, turning him into a sort of icicle yeti. He throws you down the mountain, and you wake up in a river at the base on the other side. The pathway back to the summit is the dungeon itself. When you get back to the frigid top, you fight the frozen goron warrior, needing to melt ice pillars around the arena. When you get all of them and defeat the boss, a giant icicle falls onto him, shattering the Corrupted Mask. A cult member, the one who put the mask on him, gives a message about friends in high places, and then runs off. You and the freed Goron soldier chase him to the edge of the mountain before he dives into the river below. But not being the brightest, he dropped a piece of the Mask of Resurrection.


Great Bay

The coast is being pillaged and attacked by a rogue (and quite shark-like) Zora pirate named Syzar, a descendant of Vaati who gained some of his abilities. When you meet the Zora chief, he says that Syzar is ravaging coastal villages with storms, and then looting them. These storms are getting worse and worse, and are on track to make a tidal wave strong enough to destroy the Great Bay, potentially all of Termina. You find one of Syzar's outposts and make your way through it, much like the Pirate Fortress in Majora's Mask. You need to find the location of Syzar's ship, the next dungeon. And once you make your way to the ship and get past everything, you fight Syzar. The first phase is like the Girahim battle, but with a trident instead of a sword, and the occasional wind attack. But in the second phase, he pulls out a Corrupted Mask and puts it on willingly, granting him full control over the storms. He primarily uses lightning blast attacks, and occasionally uses a cyclone that chases you around the map. When defeated, he mentions a coming darkness that will sweep the land of Termina, then beyond, before he collapses. You look through the rest of his ship, and find his treasure room. Inside is a chest containing a Mask of Resurrection piece.


Ikana

Ikana is populated by two races, the skeletal Stalchildren, and the ninja-like Garo. They are both at war, and the Stalchildren tell you that the Garo have kidnapped their princess. The distressed king sends you out on a scouting mission, where you find a Garo warrior to fight as a miniboss. But when he is defeated, he tells you that you are on the wrong side, and that the Stalchildren have taken over the Garo Stronghold. Who is telling the truth? When you find the Garo stronghold (that had been taken over by the Children of the Mask the whole time), you are immediately attacked by a skeletal creature with a slenderman figure, Stalavera, who hunts you throughout the dungeon. You can't kill her just yet, you have no choice but to evade her until you get the dungeon item. When you finally defeat her, she turns put to be the Stalchildren princess, forced to wear a Corrupted Mask. The cult members who kidnapped her give a cryptic message about their master, and his people's attack on Hyrule. Not Termina, Hyrule. The Stronghold's main tower collapses, and in the rubble you find the final piece of the Mask of Resurrection.


After all of this, back at the Astral Observatory, the Old Man gives you more information. Long ago, Majora and his followers terrorized the lands of both Hyrule and Termina, attempting to control the triforce. Together, they became known as the Dark Interlopers. They were banished to the Dark World, which later became known as the Twilight Realm. Majora became the first king of the Twilli, but being trapped in another realm, he couldn't directly fight. So he carved a mask out of the fused shadow and magically planted it in Termina, where it was found by the happy mask salesman. But that attempt failed, so his followers now want him to fight directly. The old man reveals the secret location of the Ancient Termina Mine, with magma hot enough to melt the mask fragments. When you get there and get through the dungeon, you are attacked by a giant lava monster boss. But in the chaos, the cult ambushes you and steals the fragments, using an ancient forge within the mine to fix the Mask of Resurrection. And then, they retreat to Clock Town.


The final dungeon is Clock Town itself, completely vacated by citizens and taken over by the Children of the Mask. At the top of the clock tower, you fight the cult leader. But it's too late, the ritual is complete. A massive portal opens in the sky to the Twilight Realm. The scene? Majora's grave. You and everyone else get pulled in, and the final part of the game takes place in a small portion of the Twilight realm. The final battle against Majora takes place, with three phases. Once he is defeated, peace is restored to Termina.

I think many people are overlooking a very important point: the Switch 2 isn’t simply adding a mouse function to the Joy-Con — it allows you to operate a mouse with your right hand while still controlling the controller with your left hand. Many people don’t realize what this means, but I believe it offers a completely new approach to FPS gameplay, breaking the traditional model of either using keyboard and mouse or pure controller operation. Moreover, the seamless switching between mouse mode and controller mode lets you adapt to different gameplay rhythms without having to open a menu to switch to mouse mode before a battle, and then open the menu again to switch back to controller mode before exploration or puzzle-solving. In my view, this has the potential to change the future of FPS gaming.

8:20 Reminder: Story of Seasons is actually just the Harvest Moon series, but it had to be renamed internationally due to copyright issues. The original Harvest Moon was released in 1996. Stardew Valley is heavily based on Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons, not the other way around.

Wasn't expecting Grand Bazaar to get a remake before Save the Homeland or Magical Melody, but I'm certainly not disappointed.

Edit for clarity: There are still games being released under the "Harvest Moon" title internationally, but they are being made by the original localizers of the original Harvest Moon games because they have the copyright to the Harvest Moon name and want to capitalize on that. The original Harvest Moon developers continued the series under the name Story of Seasons. So, starting in 2014, every game under the title "Harvest Moon" was made by a different developer, and the original developers have been making games under the title "Story of Seasons."

Honestly, if I ever did video essays on YouTube, the GBC&N64 and GBA&GNC Mario Golf and Tennis games would be my first three hour thing.  They made the handhelds VERY robust, story driven RPGs with a lot of cool features I’ve never seen in other games, while the home console games were essentially 3D expansion pack that just had more courses and characters to play as, but were never feature complete until you uploaded your data and CHARACTERS from the “main” games on handhelds.  In spite of that, every entry in those series that we have seen since then have been JUST the console versions, which makes them feel incomplete to me, but so many people overlook handhelds in general that they don’t realize that the reason the new ones feel hollow is because they are ACTUALLY missing something.  From the start, they were never made to be menu select golf sims: they were home hardware DLC.  

It’s a dynamic that I have literally never seen in any other set of games.

Incredible! Younger gamers won't probably realize but this game announced for a Nintendo console represents a capitulation for PlayStation in Japan.
Everybody's Golf was, alongside Gran Turismo, among SCE/SIE most popular (highest selling) first-party IP in Japan on PS1, PS2, PSP and PS3 thus it has an iconic cachet in that Country.
Also it's one of the rare PlayStation IP that has landed with at least one title on every PS console since inception: PS1, PS2, PSP, PS3, PSV, PS4 (even PSVR) and now, with this new multi-platform game, PS5 too.

Watch it being announced in a Nintendo Direct is surreal for us gamers of the earlier times.

For anyone that may be confused, this is my best understanding of this announcement. 

This is essentially just allowing you to swap the license between two systems for games that you own on your Nintendo account. Right now, if you were to try and play a digital game on a secondary switch, it would need to verify your license by connecting to the internet. If you don’t have internet, you can’t play the game (again, this is only an issue for a switch that is registered as a secondary). 

[EDIT TO THE ABOVE: I now think this is more of converting your games into virtual cards (yes, I know that’s the whole point), but you are *possibly* removing access to the game on one system if you load it onto another. As if you were removing a physical card. So you will need to make sure to “insert” the virtual cards onto the system you want to play the game, if it’s not already loaded there.]

Swapping the virtual card to that secondary switch will then allow you to open that game offline and anywhere. 

This is also not a replacement for the current “game sharing” that we have now. As the disclaimer at the end states, “By navigating to your user settings -> online digital license (close enough) and turning the setting ON, you can opt to connect to the internet to start software.”

So I hope this is correct and clears up any confusion anyone might have.

EDIT: After discussing with some friends and reading other comments. There is a possibility this is an alternative to the current system we have of digital games. Cause as the disclaimer states, you’re opting in or out of the online connection for games. So you can make the choice to convert your games to virtual cards, or don’t change anything at all (obviously allowing you to toggle between the two in the settings). This is just another possibility.

Also, this is all my best guess with the information given, so I apologize if any information I have said proves to be false later on.

The share LASTS FOR 2 WEEKS before whoever you shared it with loses access. It's a direct equivalent to letting your friend borrow a physical game card you have, but for a DIGITAL GAME YOU OWN. 

It's not a way to transfer all of your games to your new Switch (unless you want to have to keep redoing the share every 2 weeks). It's not a replacement for physical game cards. It's also not something that will make install sizes smaller, because the full digital game will just be installed on the 2nd device like it is on the original device the game is on.

Edit: people corrected me about some important stuff I misunderstood. Sharing to a device you own has no time limit on the share and you can transfer back with no restrictions. It's sharing to a friend in your Nintendo Family that lasts 2 weeks. The other points still stand about it being for digital games and all though. Thanks for the info guys fr
